title: Valid Palindrome
statement:
Decide whether a line of text is a palindrome when you look only at its letters and digits.

The input is one line of text, which can be empty. Skip every character that is not a letter or a digit, like spaces and punctuation, and treat uppercase and lowercase letters as the same. Print `true` when what is left reads the same forward and backward and `false` otherwise. A line with no letters or digits prints `true`. Try to check the line where it is, without building a cleaned-up copy.

Input:

```text
A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
```

Expected output:

```text
true
```

tests.stdin: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

hints: Put one index at the first character and one at the last, and move them toward each other.

When the character under an index is not a letter or a digit, move that index past it without comparing anything. Your language can tell you whether a character is a letter or a digit (in JavaScript and TypeScript, test it with a regular expression like `/[a-z0-9]/i`).
Compare the two characters in lowercase. As soon as they differ, the line is not a palindrome. When the indexes meet, it is.
